blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In practice, British indirectness is less about hiding things and more about protecting relationships while still getting the message across. When your manager says "I wonder if we could just take another look at this?", they are almost certainly asking for real changes — not a second glance.

The trick, when you hear this kind of phrase, is to slow down and translate it in your head. Replace the soft phrase with the direct one, and ask yourself whether that changes what you should do next. It usually does.

What really helps is asking a quiet follow-up question: "Could you tell me, roughly, what you'd like to see different?" That gives the speaker permission to be a little more specific, without forcing them to break the polite register. It almost always works — and the answer is almost always much clearer than the first sentence.

items.q: According to the text, British indirectness is mainly about…
options: protecting relationships while still getting the message across
items.why: "less about hiding things and more about protecting relationships while still getting the message across."

items.q: When a manager says "I wonder if we could just take another look at this?", they are probably asking for…
items.why: "they are almost certainly asking for real changes — not a second glance."

items.q: What does the text recommend you do when you hear a soft phrase?
options: Ignore it until it is repeated
Escalate it to a senior colleague
Reply immediately in the same polite register
Slow down and translate it into the direct version in your head
items.why: "the trick… is to slow down and translate it in your head."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Translating the phrase changes what you do next.
Soft phrasing often carries a firm expectation.
A follow-up question can reveal the real request.
You should take polite feedback at face value and move on.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo argumenta o contrário — não se deve levar a frase polida ao pé da letra.

items.q: Why does a quiet follow-up question work so well, according to the text?
options: It gives the speaker permission to be more specific without breaking the polite register
It forces the speaker to abandon politeness
items.why: "That gives the speaker permission to be a little more specific, without forcing them to break the polite register."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte orientando o analista júnior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, sit with me for a second — I read the email your manager sent you, and I can see why you thought it was positive. But let me walk you through it.

He wrote, "This is a really solid start, I wonder if we could just revisit the second section when you have a moment." Now, to your ear that sounds like a small tweak. In practice, "revisit" plus "a really solid start" almost always means: the second section needs a full rewrite. The kind words are there to protect you, not to tell you everything is fine.

So here is what I'd do. Don't panic, and don't rewrite blindly either. Send one short, calm follow-up: "Thanks — could you tell me roughly what you'd like to see different in that section?" That gives him room to be specific without dropping the polite tone.

Nine times out of ten, the reply comes back much clearer than the first message. And you'll have saved yourself two days of guessing. The skill isn't writing faster — it's learning to slow down and translate what people actually mean.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

options: It contained kind words like "a really solid start"
items.why: "I can see why you thought it was positive… 'a really solid start'."

items.why: "'revisit' plus 'a really solid start' almost always means: the second section needs a full rewrite."

items.q: What does Charlotte advise the analyst to do?
options: Ask another colleague to interpret it
Send a short, calm follow-up question
items.why: "Send one short, calm follow-up: 'could you tell me roughly what you'd like to see different?'"

options: Slowing down and translating what people actually mean

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "His feedback was so indirect that half the team missed the point." Indirect means…
options: not stated in a plain, straightforward way
items.why: Indirect = indireto: a mensagem não é dita de forma direta e clara.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A calm ___ question like 'what would you like to see different?' unlocks the real request."
items.why: Follow-up question = pergunta complementar, que faz o interlocutor detalhar.

items.q: "He kept the polite register even while turning the whole plan down." Here register means…
options: the level or style of language used
items.why: Register = registro: o nível/estilo de linguagem (formal, polido, informal).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I didn't need the full detail — just a ___ idea of what she wanted."
items.why: Rough idea = ideia geral, aproximada, sem todos os detalhes.

items.q: "When feedback is vague, slow down before you react." To slow down here means to…
options: take your time and think before acting
items.why: To slow down = ir com calma, pensar antes de reagir.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando você decodifica feedback educado. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "I wonder if we could take another look at the second section." In British feedback this usually means…
options: read it aloud in the meeting
the section is perfect as it is
items.why: "Take another look at" no registro britânico costuma sinalizar que mudanças de verdade são esperadas.

items.q: "She didn't say no; she pushed back on the timeline instead." To push back on means to…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Before we send it out, the director has to sign off on the report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Let's circle back on the wording once you've spoken to him." To circle back means to…
items.why: Circle back = retomar um assunto mais tarde.

items.q: "They loved the idea but never followed through on the edits." They…
options: failed to carry the edits to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; "never followed through" = não concluíram.
